title: My Feelings at School

themePack.overview: Toddlers practice noticing big feelings at school—happy, sad, mad, scared, and calm—through mirrors, short stories, puppets, and repeatable calm-down games. Each day offers one clear feeling focus with simple words, large washable materials, and process-first art (no perfect crafts). Teachers model naming feelings, gentle helping, and quick reset strategies so toddlers build security with classmates and caregivers.
themePack.materials:
Emotion picture cards (happy, sad, mad, scared, calm)
Child-safe handheld mirrors
Soft puppets and stuffed animals
Feelings chart at toddler height
Washable crayons, markers, and paint
Large paper / construction paper
Glue sticks and yarn scraps (optional)
Scarves and bean bags
Feathers or pinwheels for breathing practice
Calm-down bottles (securely sealed; no loose beads for mouthing)
Play dough
Music player for freeze/dance transitions
Smocks, wipes, and a quiet calm corner mat
themePack.family: Each evening, ask “What feeling visited you at school today?” Offer two choices if needed (“happy or tired?”). Practice one calm strategy together—three feather breaths or a cozy hug count. Celebrate any feeling talk; naming emotions at home helps toddlers use the same words with teachers and friends.
milestones: Language: Uses or approximates feeling words (happy, sad, mad, calm) with gesture or picture support
SEL: Notices a peer’s feeling and tries a kind action with teacher coaching
Motor: Imitates simple face motions, dance freezes, and fine-motor process art marks
Cognition: Matches a face card to a feeling word and recalls one calm-down choice

songs.title: Feelings Face Chant
songs.lyrics:
Happy face, happy face, smile so wide,
Sad face, sad face, tears we can dry.
Mad face, mad face, stomp then rest,
Calm face, calm face—breathe is best.
songs.motions: Show each face on cue; gentle cheek wipe motion for sad; two soft stomps then hands on heart for mad/rest; hands on belly for breathe.
songs.teacherDirections: Hold matching emotion cards while chanting. Invite toddlers to copy faces in mirrors. Keep stomps soft and brief; move quickly into calm breathing.
songs.whenToUse: Morning circle with the Feelings Chart; before Feelings Match-Up
songs.transitionPurpose: Preview today’s feeling vocabulary and settle into circle

songs.title: Breathe In, Blow Soft
songs.lyrics:
Breathe in slow, breathe out soft,
Shoulders down, hands aloft.
Breathe in slow, blow a feather,
Calm comes back—we feel better.
songs.motions: Hands on belly for breathe in; soft blow toward a feather/pinwheel; shoulders drop; hands rest in lap on better.
songs.teacherDirections: Use during Calm Breathing with Feathers or Pinwheel Breathing. Model one breath at a time. Offer a quiet alternative (hand on heart) if blowing is hard.
songs.whenToUse: After big energy, conflict coaching, or before rest
songs.transitionPurpose: Reset bodies and voices toward calm

songs.title: If You're Happy and You Know It
songs.lyrics:
If you're happy and you know it, clap your hands.
If you're happy and you know it, clap your hands.
If you're happy and you know it, then your face will surely show it.
If you're happy and you know it, clap your hands.

(Additional verses teachers may use: If you're mad… stomp once then rest. If you're calm… breathe in slow.)
songs.motions: Clap; for mad verse one soft stomp then hands on heart; for calm verse belly breaths—avoid long stomping chains.
songs.teacherDirections: Keep verses short. Prefer original Feelings Face Chant for deeper emotion practice; use this traditional song for joyful participation only. Do not invent copyrighted pop song variants.
songs.whenToUse: Happy Dance Party or outdoor Happy Walk warm-up

books.title: The Color Monster
books.author: Anna Llenas
books.why: Colors mapped to feelings give toddlers a concrete way to sort and name emotions at school.
before: What color feels happy to you today?
during: Which feeling is the monster showing on this page?
after: What feeling might you put in a jar today?
books.substitute: Use emotion color cards and Feelings Face Chant if the book is unavailable.

books.title: Glad Monster, Sad Monster
books.author: Ed Emberley & Anne Miranda
books.why: Flip-style monster faces make happy/sad talk playful and easy to imitate with mirrors.
before: Can you make a glad face in the mirror?
during: Is this monster glad or sad?
after: Tell a friend one thing that makes you glad at school.
books.substitute: Mirror, Mirror, Happy Me with glad/sad cards.

books.title: Llama Llama Misses Mama
books.author: Anna Dewdney
books.why: Separation feelings are familiar for toddlers starting or returning to school; the story normalizes missing and reconnecting.
before: Have you ever missed someone at school?
during: How does Llama Llama feel right now?
after: What helps you feel brave when you miss someone?
books.substitute: Helping Teddy Feel Brave with a short teacher story about missing and reuniting.

books.title: Today I Feel Silly
books.author: Jamie Lee Curtis
books.why: Many feelings in one story expand vocabulary beyond happy/sad for curious toddlers.
before: What feeling word do you want to listen for?
during: Show me that feeling with your face.
after: Which feeling from the book did you notice today?
books.substitute: Optional enrichment title—if time is short, keep the top three books; use feeling cards for a mini walk.

books.title: Grumpy Monkey
books.author: Suzanne Lang
books.why: Validates mad/grumpy days and models that friends can still care without forcing fake smiles.
before: Is it okay to feel grumpy sometimes?
during: What does Jim Panzee need from friends?
after: What helps you when you feel grumpy at school?
books.substitute: Optional fifth title—enrich fully only if schedule allows; otherwise note for family lending library.

printableIdeas.title: School Feelings Picture Card Pack
printableIdeas.purpose: Large happy/sad/mad/scared/calm cards for chart work, matching, freeze dance cues, and calm-corner visuals.

printableIdeas.title: Calm Choice Cards
printableIdeas.purpose: Picture choices (breathe, hug a teddy, ask a teacher, drink water) used after Helping the Mad Monster and Pinwheel Breathing.

teacherTips: Process focus: open-ended marks and stickers are enough—no identical bulletin-board faces required.
Offer blank circles instead of rigid templates when possible.
Tearing is the fine-motor goal; finished hearts will look different and that is celebrated.
Use large feathers; supervise closely; offer pinwheels or hand-on-belly for children who should not mouth feathers.
Call feeling words instead of copyrighted song hooks; freeze on calm card.
Keep paths clear; soft knees on freezes.
Coach kind helping language; keep monster play playful, not scary.
Practice one calm choice after the story play.

themePack.safetyNotes: Use child-safe mirrors and securely sealed calm bottles—no loose water beads or small parts that toddlers might mouth. Washable, large materials preferred. Art is process-based with smocks and wipeable surfaces. Supervise breathing props; provide non-mouthing alternatives. Keep emotional coaching inclusive: all feelings are welcome, and no child is forced to perform a feeling face for photos.

notes: Replaced copyrighted-risk songs (Baby Shark Feelings Version, The Feelings Song, Skidamarink) with original LLH chants plus one traditional PD option. Book authors cleaned from catalog (Anna Llenas; Ed Emberley & Anne Miranda; Anna Dewdney; Jamie Lee Curtis; Suzanne Lang). Top 3 books fully enriched; titles 4–5 noted as optional enrichment.
